questions.question: Each student that enrolls at a school is assigned a unique ID stored as a binary number. The ID numbers increase sequentially by 1. If the last student's ID was 1001 0011, what binary number will be assigned to the next student?
questions.explanation: 1001 0011 in decimal is 147. Adding 1 gives 148, which is 1001 0100 in binary.

questions.question: What is the decimal value of the binary number 1011 0110?
What is the binary representation of the decimal number 45?
The same sequence of bits 01000001 is interpreted differently by two programs — one displays 65 and another displays the letter 'A'. Which of the following best explains this?

options.A: One of the programs has a logic error
options.B: The same sequence of bits may represent different types of data in different contexts
options.C: Binary numbers can only represent integers so the letter A must be stored differently
options.D: The two programs are using different number bases

questions.explanation: The same sequence of bits may represent different types of data in different contexts. 01000001 represents 65 as an integer and 'A' as a character depending on how it is interpreted.

questions.question: A programmer stores the result of dividing 1 by 3. The program displays 0.3333333 instead of the exact value. Which of the following best explains this?

options.A: An overflow error because the result is too large
options.B: A round-off error because the fixed number of bits used to represent real numbers limits precision
options.C: A logic error because the programmer used the wrong operator
options.D: A syntax error because division produces a decimal that cannot be stored

questions.explanation: A round-off error occurs because the fixed number of bits used to represent real numbers limits precision. Some real numbers can only be stored as approximations.

questions.stimulus: A programmer stores the value 200 using a fixed number of bits that can only represent values from 0 to 255. The programmer then adds 100 to this value.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes what will happen?

options.A: The program displays 300 because addition always produces the correct result
options.B: The program displays 255 because that is the maximum value
options.C: An overflow error occurs because 300 exceeds the defined range of values
options.D: A round-off error occurs because 300 cannot be stored precisely

questions.explanation: An overflow error occurs when a computer attempts to handle a number outside the defined range of values. Since 300 exceeds the maximum of 255, an overflow error occurs.

questions.question: A music streaming service stores songs digitally. The original recordings were analog. Which of the following best describes how analog audio is converted to digital data?

options.A: The analog audio is compressed using a lossless algorithm
options.B: The analog audio is sampled at regular intervals and each sample is stored as a sequence of bits
options.C: The analog audio is converted to text and encoded in binary using ASCII
options.D: The analog audio is stored as a continuous wave function represented by a single binary value

questions.explanation: Analog data can be approximated digitally using a sampling technique — measuring values of the analog signal at regular intervals. The samples are measured to determine the exact bits required to store each sample.

questions.question: How many bits are in 4 bytes?
questions.explanation: A byte is 8 bits. 4 bytes × 8 bits = 32 bits.

questions.question: A student claims that digital data is a perfect representation of real-world analog data. Which of the following best evaluates this claim?

options.A: The claim is correct because sampling captures every detail
options.B: The claim is correct because bits can represent any value precisely
options.C: The claim is incorrect because digital data approximates analog data and the fixed number of bits limits precision
options.D: The claim is incorrect because computers cannot store analog data in any form

questions.explanation: Digital data approximates analog data through sampling — it is not a perfect representation. The fixed number of bits limits precision, which is why round-off errors occur.

questions.stimulus: A photographer needs to send high-resolution images to a client for large-format printing. The images must be delivered at full quality. However the file sizes are too large to send by email.
questions.question: Which compression approach would be MOST appropriate?

options.A: Lossy compression, because it reduces file size more than lossless
options.B: Lossy compression, because the client can restore original quality after receiving the files
options.C: Lossless compression, because it guarantees complete reconstruction of the original data
options.D: Lossless compression, because it always produces smaller files than lossy compression

questions.explanation: In situations where quality or the ability to reconstruct the original is maximally important, lossless compression is typically chosen. Lossless guarantees complete reconstruction, which is essential for print-quality images.

questions.stimulus: A video streaming service needs to transmit live sports to millions of users simultaneously. Slight reductions in video quality are acceptable as long as the video streams smoothly.
questions.question: Which compression approach would be MOST appropriate?

options.A: Lossless compression, because it preserves all original data for highest quality
options.B: Lossless compression, because it transmits data faster than lossy compression
options.C: Lossy compression, because it reduces file size more and minimizes transmission time
options.D: Lossy compression, because it guarantees complete reconstruction of the original video

questions.explanation: In situations where minimizing data size or transmission time is maximally important, lossy compression is typically chosen. Lossy can reduce bits more than lossless, ideal for live streaming.

questions.question: A text file is compressed from 400 KB to 250 KB using a lossless algorithm. Which of the following is true about the compressed file?

options.A: It contains less information than the original because it has fewer bits
options.B: It can be fully restored to the original 400 KB file
options.C: It will lose some formatting when decompressed
options.D: It uses lossy compression because the file size decreased significantly

questions.explanation: Lossless compression guarantees complete reconstruction of the original data. Fewer bits does not necessarily mean less information.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why lossy compression can usually reduce file sizes more than lossless compression?

options.A: Lossy compression uses a more powerful computer
options.B: Lossy compression only stores every other bit of the original data
options.C: Lossy compression permanently removes some data, allowing greater size reduction at the cost of only reconstructing an approximation
options.D: Lossy compression converts data to a more efficient format that lossless cannot use

questions.explanation: Lossy compression permanently discards some data, achieving greater size reduction than lossless which must preserve all original data.

questions.stimulus:
Biologists attach tracking collars to wild animals. For each animal the following data are collected at frequent intervals:
- The time
- The date
- The location of the animal
questions.question: Which of the following questions about an animal could NOT be answered using only this data?

options.A: Approximately how many miles did the animal travel in one week?
options.B: Does the animal travel in groups with other tracked animals?
options.C: Do the movement patterns of the animal vary according to the weather?
options.D: In what geographic locations does the animal typically travel?

questions.explanation: The tracking collars only collect time, date, and location. Weather data is not collected, so questions about how movement patterns relate to weather cannot be answered using only this data.

questions.stimulus: A researcher analyzes data from 10,000 students and finds that students who eat breakfast score higher on standardized tests than students who skip breakfast.
questions.question: Which of the following conclusions is best supported by this finding?

options.A: Eating breakfast causes students to score higher on standardized tests
options.B: Students who want to improve test scores should start eating breakfast
options.C: There is a correlation between eating breakfast and higher test scores, but this does not necessarily indicate causation
options.D: The data proves that breakfast is the most important factor in academic performance

questions.explanation: A correlation found in data does not necessarily indicate a causal relationship. Additional research is needed to understand the exact nature of the relationship.

questions.stimulus:
A photo taken on a smartphone has the following associated information:
- File name: vacation.jpg
- File size: 4.2 MB
- Date taken: July 4, 2024
- Location: 40.7128° N, 74.0060° W
- Camera model: Smartphone X Pro
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the file size, date taken, location, and camera model?

options.A: Primary data, because they describe important properties of the photo
options.B: Metadata, because they are data about the photo rather than the photo itself
options.C: Compressed data, because they represent the photo in a smaller form
options.D: Filtered data, because they were selected from a larger set

questions.explanation: Metadata are data about data. The photo is the primary data, while the file size, date, location, and camera model are metadata — they describe properties of the photo without being the photo itself.

questions.stimulus:
A photo taken on a smartphone has the following associated information:
- File name: vacation.jpg
- File size: 4.2 MB
- Date taken: July 4, 2024
- Location: 40.7128° N, 74.0060° W
- Camera model: Smartphone X Pro
questions.question: A user changes the file name from vacation.jpg to beach_trip.jpg. Which of the following best describes the effect?

options.A: The photo itself is changed because the file name is part of the image data
options.B: The metadata is changed but the primary data remains unchanged
options.C: Both the metadata and the photo are changed because they are stored together
options.D: The photo is compressed because renaming a file reduces its size

questions.explanation: Changes and deletions made to metadata do not change the primary data. The file name is metadata — changing it does not alter the photo itself.

questions.stimulus: A researcher collects survey responses about favorite colors from 500 students. The data contains entries like: 'blue', 'Blue', 'BLUE', 'blu', and 'light blue' — all intended to mean the same color.
questions.question: Which process is needed to fix this before analyzing the data?

options.A: Data compression, to reduce the number of bits needed
options.B: Data filtering, to remove responses that don't match the expected format
options.C: Data cleaning, to make the data uniform without changing its meaning
options.D: Data sampling, to select a representative subset

questions.explanation: Data cleaning is the process of making data uniform without changing its meaning — replacing all equivalent abbreviations, spellings, and capitalizations with the same word.

questions.question: A hospital collects health data only from patients who visit its clinics in wealthy urban neighborhoods. A researcher uses this data to draw conclusions about the health of the general population. Which of the following best identifies the problem?

options.A: The data set is too large to process accurately
options.B: The data needs to be cleaned before analysis
options.C: The data contains bias because the source only represents a specific subset of the population
options.D: The researcher should collect more data from the same source to eliminate bias

questions.explanation: Problems of bias are often created by the type or source of data being collected. Bias is not eliminated by simply collecting more data from the same biased source.

questions.question: A research team is analyzing 10 billion social media posts on a single computer and finds it takes weeks to process. Which of the following best explains this challenge?

options.A: The data set contains bias that slows processing speed
options.B: Large data sets are difficult to process using a single computer and may require parallel systems
options.C: The data needs to be cleaned before it can be processed efficiently
options.D: Social media data cannot be analyzed using standard computing tools

questions.explanation: Large data sets are difficult to process using a single computer and may require parallel systems. Scalability is an important consideration when working with large data sets.

questions.stimulus: A teacher has a spreadsheet with names, grades, and attendance for 150 students. The teacher wants to identify only the students who have both a grade below 70 and more than 5 absences.
questions.question: Which process best describes what the teacher needs to do?

options.A: Transform the data by adding a letter grade column
options.B: Filter the data to keep only students who meet both conditions
options.C: Visualize the data by creating a chart showing grade distribution
options.D: Combine the data with another source to add more student information

questions.explanation: Filtering a data set means keeping only the elements that meet a given condition. The teacher needs to filter for students with grade below 70 AND more than 5 absences.

questions.question: A data analyst doubles every value in a list of monthly revenue figures to project doubled sales. Which of the following best describes this process?

options.A: Filtering, because the analyst is selecting specific values
options.B: Combining, because the analyst is merging two lists
options.C: Transforming, because the analyst is applying an operation to every element
options.D: Visualizing, because the analyst is creating a projection

questions.explanation: Transforming a data set means applying an operation to every element, such as doubling every number in a list.

questions.question: A programmer writes a program to analyze sales data. After the first run, results suggest weekends have higher sales. The programmer refines the program to compare weekend sales by season and discovers summer weekends are highest. Which of the following best describes this process?

options.A: The programmer is using lossless compression to reduce the size of the data
options.B: The programmer is using programs in an iterative and interactive way to gain deeper insight from the data
options.C: The programmer is cleaning the data to remove invalid records
options.D: The programmer is filtering the data to remove weekday sales

questions.explanation: Programs are used in an iterative and interactive way when processing information to allow users to gain insight and knowledge about data.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between data compression and information?

options.A: Fewer bits always means less information
options.B: Fewer bits does not necessarily mean less information because compression removes redundancy not meaning
options.C: More bits always means more information
options.D: Fewer bits always means more information because compression makes data more efficient

questions.explanation: Fewer bits does not necessarily mean less information. Lossless compression can produce a smaller file that still contains all the original information.

questions.question: A social media platform collects data about users' posts, likes, and browsing history. A researcher notices that users who post frequently also tend to have more followers. Which of the following best describes this finding?

options.A: Posting frequently causes users to gain more followers
options.B: Having more followers causes users to post more frequently
options.C: There is a correlation between posting frequency and follower count, but this does not necessarily indicate causation
options.D: The data proves that posting more is always the best strategy for gaining followers

questions.explanation: A correlation found in data does not necessarily indicate causation. Additional research is needed — other factors like content quality could explain both.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how metadata increases the effective use of data?

options.A: Metadata compresses the primary data to make it easier to store
options.B: Metadata provides additional context that allows data to be structured, organized, and found more easily
options.C: Metadata replaces the primary data when the original file is too large
options.D: Metadata filters out invalid or duplicate entries from a data set

questions.explanation: Metadata can increase the effective use of data by providing additional information. Metadata allow data to be structured and organized and are used for finding, organizing, and managing information.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes abstraction in the context of how computers represent data?

options.A: The process of converting decimal numbers to binary for storage
options.B: The process of reducing complexity by grouping bits to represent higher-level concepts like numbers, characters, and color rather than working with individual bits
options.C: The process of compressing data to reduce the number of bits needed
options.D: The process of sampling analog data at regular intervals

questions.explanation: Abstraction is the process of reducing complexity by focusing on the main idea. Grouping bits to represent numbers, characters, and color is abstraction — it hides irrelevant details of individual bits.

questions.question: A programmer is building a program to help a school identify at-risk students. The program combines attendance records, grade data, and counselor notes. After the first version, the programmer discovers it misses some students and adds a new data source. Which of the following best describes this approach?

options.A: The programmer is cleaning the data by removing invalid records
options.B: The programmer is compressing the data to make the program run faster
options.C: The programmer is using programs in an iterative and interactive way to improve insight from the data
options.D: The programmer is filtering the data to keep only at-risk students

questions.explanation: Programs are used in an iterative and interactive way when processing information. The programmer builds, tests, refines, and retests — each cycle improving the program's ability to gain insight.

questions.question: A student compresses an image using lossy compression and sends it to a friend. The friend wants to restore the image to its original quality. Which of the following best describes what will happen?

options.A: The friend can fully restore the original because compression is always reversible
options.B: The friend can partially restore the image by applying lossless decompression
options.C: The friend cannot fully restore the original because lossy compression only allows reconstruction of an approximation
options.D: The friend cannot restore the image at all because lossy compression permanently destroys the file

questions.explanation: Lossy compression only allows reconstruction of an approximation of the original data. Once data is discarded through lossy compression, the original cannot be fully recovered.

questions.question: A researcher wants to determine which neighborhoods have the highest rates of childhood asthma. Which TWO data sources would MOST likely need to be combined? Select the best single answer.

options.A: Hospital asthma diagnosis records and a list of all elementary schools
options.B: Hospital asthma diagnosis records with patient addresses AND air quality measurements by neighborhood
options.C: A survey of parents about outdoor activities AND air quality measurements by neighborhood
options.D: Hospital records AND a list of all elementary schools

questions.explanation: Often a single source does not contain all the data needed. Hospital records identify where asthma cases occur and air quality data helps explain why — combining these allows the researcher to identify both highest-rate neighborhoods and potential causes.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a challenge that exists for data sets regardless of their size?

options.A: All data sets require parallel computing systems to process
options.B: All data sets need to be compressed before analysis
options.C: Data sets may contain incomplete, invalid, or non-uniform data that requires cleaning
options.D: All data sets require specialized hardware to store

questions.explanation: Data sets pose challenges regardless of size, such as the need to clean data, incomplete data, invalid data, and the need to combine data sources. These challenges exist for both small and large data sets.

questions.question: A data analyst creates a bar chart showing monthly sales figures for the past year. Which process best describes what the analyst is doing?

options.A: Filtering — keeping only the relevant months
options.B: Transforming — converting the data to a different format
options.C: Visualizing — representing data through a chart to communicate insight
options.D: Combining — merging multiple data sources into one

questions.explanation: Tables, diagrams, text, and other visual tools can be used to communicate insight and knowledge gained from data. Creating a bar chart is visualizing the data.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why scalability is an important consideration when designing systems to process data?

options.A: Scalable systems can clean data automatically
options.B: Scalable systems can compress data more efficiently
options.C: The computational capacity of a system affects how data sets can be processed and stored as their size grows
options.D: Scalable systems eliminate bias by processing all data sources equally

questions.explanation: Scalability of systems is an important consideration because the computational capacity of a system affects how data sets can be processed and stored. As data sets grow larger, systems must scale to handle them.

questions.question: A news organization wants to predict election results using data from online polls. A data scientist warns the predictions may not be accurate. Which of the following best supports the data scientist's concern?

options.A: Online polls collect too much data to analyze accurately
options.B: Online polls may introduce bias because they only capture opinions of people who choose to participate online, which may not represent all voters
options.C: Online data cannot be cleaned because responses are anonymous
options.D: The data is too large to process before the election

questions.explanation: Problems of bias are often created by the type or source of data being collected. Online polls only reach people with Internet access who choose to participate, which may not represent all voters. Bias is not eliminated by collecting more data from the same biased source.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the binary place value system?

options.A: Each position has a place value equal to 2 multiplied by the position number
options.B: The place value of each position is 2 raised to the power of the position, with positions numbered starting at 0 on the right
options.C: Each position has a place value equal to 10 raised to the power of the position
options.D: All positions have the same place value of 2

questions.explanation: The place value of each position is determined by the base (2) raised to the power of the position. Positions are numbered starting at 0 on the rightmost digit. So positions are worth 1, 2, 4, 8, 16... from right to left.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains why a single data source may be insufficient to draw a conclusion?

options.A: Single data sources always contain bias
options.B: A single source may not contain all the data needed — combining data from multiple sources may be necessary to formulate a conclusion
options.C: Single data sources can only be used for small-scale research
options.D: Single data sources always contain incomplete data

questions.explanation: Often a single source does not contain the data needed to draw a conclusion. It may be necessary to combine data from a variety of sources to formulate a conclusion.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST example of using programs to gain insight from data?

options.A: Using a word processor to write a report about customer behavior
options.B: Using a spreadsheet to sort customer names alphabetically
options.C: Using a program to cluster customer purchase data and identify groups with similar buying habits
options.D: Using a calculator to add up monthly revenue figures manually

questions.explanation: Combining data sources, clustering data, and classifying data are parts of the process of using programs to gain insight and knowledge from data. Clustering customers by buying habits extracts meaningful patterns from data.

questions.question: Which of the following binary numbers has the greatest decimal value?

A city government wants to study traffic patterns to reduce congestion. They have data from traffic cameras but find it is not enough to identify root causes. Which of the following would MOST help improve their analysis?

options.A: Cleaning the existing traffic camera data to remove duplicate entries
options.B: Combining the traffic camera data with public transit ridership data and weather records
options.C: Compressing the traffic camera data to reduce storage requirements
options.D: Collecting more traffic camera data from the same locations

questions.explanation: Often a single source does not contain all the data needed. Combining traffic camera data with transit ridership and weather records provides additional context that may reveal causes of congestion that camera data alone cannot show.

questions.question: A researcher archives 10 years of satellite images for future scientific study. Storage space is limited but the images must be available at full quality. Which of the following best describes the tradeoff the researcher faces?

options.A: Using lossy compression saves more space but sacrifices the ability to fully reconstruct the original images for accurate analysis
options.B: Using lossless compression saves more space and guarantees full reconstruction
options.C: Using lossy compression saves more space and still guarantees full reconstruction
options.D: Using lossless compression sacrifices quality but saves more space than lossy

questions.explanation: Lossy compression achieves greater size reduction but only allows reconstruction of an approximation. For scientific analysis where exact data is needed, this tradeoff may be unacceptable.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists the processes that can be used to extract or modify information from data?

options.A: Transforming, filtering, combining or comparing, and visualizing
options.B: Compressing, cleaning, filtering, and sampling
options.C: Sorting, searching, filtering, and encrypting
options.D: Collecting, storing, deleting, and archiving

questions.explanation: The CED identifies transforming every element, filtering a data set, combining or comparing data, and visualizing a data set as the processes that can be used to extract or modify information from data.

questions.question: A programmer has employee records from three different offices and wants to find patterns in performance across all offices combined. Which process would she use first?

options.A: Filtering to remove employees with incomplete records
options.B: Visualizing to create a chart of all employee performance
options.C: Combining to merge records from all three offices into one data set
options.D: Transforming to convert all performance ratings to a percentage scale

questions.explanation: Before analyzing patterns across all offices, the records from the three separate sources must be combined into one data set. Combining data sources is a fundamental step in using programs to gain insight.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of analog data?

options.A: The binary representation of a student ID number
options.B: The number of students enrolled in a class
options.C: The volume of a song as it gradually fades out
options.D: A list of test scores stored in a spreadsheet

questions.explanation: Analog data have values that change smoothly rather than in discrete intervals over time. The volume of a song gradually fading is analog — it changes continuously. ID numbers and enrollment counts are discrete values.

questions.question: A company surveys customers about their satisfaction using an open text field. Responses include 'Great', 'great', 'GREAT', 'gr8', and 'Good'. Which challenge does this data present?

options.A: The data set is too large to process on a single computer
options.B: The data contains bias because only satisfied customers responded
options.C: The data is not uniform because users expressed similar sentiments in different ways
options.D: The data cannot be analyzed because it contains text rather than numbers

questions.explanation: When users enter data into an open field, the way they abbreviate, spell, or capitalize may vary. This non-uniform data requires cleaning to make it uniform without changing its meaning before analysis.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are examples of analog data?

options.A: The binary representation of a student's ID number
options.B: The pitch of a violin note as it gradually increases
options.C: The number of students enrolled in a class
options.D: The temperature of a room as it slowly rises throughout the day

questions.explanation: Analog data have values that change smoothly rather than in discrete intervals. Pitch gradually increasing and temperature slowly rising are both analog. A binary ID and enrollment count are discrete values.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following situations would most likely call for lossless compression?

options.A: Compressing music files for a streaming service where users listen on phone speakers
options.B: Compressing a patient's medical scan images that doctors will use to diagnose a condition
options.C: Compressing a legal contract that must be archived and retrieved exactly as written
options.D: Compressing video files for social media where slight quality reduction is acceptable

questions.explanation: Lossless compression is chosen when quality or exact reconstruction is maximally important. Medical scans must be preserved exactly for accurate diagnosis, and legal documents must be retrievable exactly as written.

questions.stimulus: A hospital is building a system to store and transmit two types of files: (1) patient X-ray images used by doctors for diagnosis, and (2) short video messages patients send to their doctors describing symptoms.
questions.question:
Part A: For each file type, identify which compression algorithm — lossless or lossy — would be most appropriate. Explain your reasoning for each choice.

Part B: A doctor argues that both file types should use lossless compression to preserve maximum quality. Evaluate this argument.
questions.rubric:
PART A (2 points):
Award 1 point for correctly identifying lossless for X-ray images AND explaining why: X-ray images are used for medical diagnosis where quality and exact reconstruction are maximally important — any loss could affect diagnosis accuracy.
Award 1 point for correctly identifying lossy for patient video messages AND explaining why: slight quality reduction is acceptable for symptom videos — minimizing transmission time is more important than perfect quality.

PART B (2 points):
Award 1 point for acknowledging that the doctor's reasoning makes sense for X-ray images where quality is critical.
Award 1 point for explaining why it is not necessary for video messages: lossy compression would achieve greater size reduction for videos where slight quality loss is imperceptible and acceptable, saving storage and transmission costs without meaningful quality impact. In situations where minimizing data size is maximally important, lossy compression is typically chosen.

questions.stimulus: A researcher studies the relationship between hours of sleep and academic performance in high school students. After analyzing data from 2,000 students at private schools in one city, the researcher finds that students who sleep more than 8 hours per night have higher GPAs on average than students who sleep less than 6 hours.
questions.question:
Part A: Identify what type of relationship the researcher has found. Explain whether this finding alone is sufficient to conclude that sleeping more causes higher GPA.

Part B: Identify one way the data source may introduce bias into the researcher's conclusions. Explain how this bias could affect the validity of conclusions about all high school students.

Part C: Describe one additional data source the researcher could combine with this data to strengthen their conclusions.
questions.rubric:
PART A (2 points):
Award 1 point for identifying the relationship as a correlation.
Award 1 point for explaining that correlation does not prove causation — additional research is needed to understand the exact nature of the relationship.

PART B (2 points):
Award 1 point for identifying a specific bias: data collected only from private school students in one city may not represent all high school students — private school students may have more resources, parental support, or consistent schedules.
Award 1 point for explaining the effect: bias is not eliminated by collecting more data from the same biased source — conclusions drawn from this data may not apply to public school students, students in other cities, or students with different socioeconomic backgrounds.

PART C (1 point):
Award 1 point for identifying a relevant additional data source. Accept: data from public school students in diverse cities; data including students of different income levels; data from multiple geographic regions.

questions.stimulus: Each student at a school is assigned a unique ID stored as an 8-bit binary number. Currently the school has 200 students.
questions.question:
Part A: What is the decimal value of the binary student ID 1100 1010?

Part B: How many unique student IDs can be represented using 8 bits? Explain your reasoning.

Part C: The school is planning to expand and expects to eventually have 300 students. Explain whether the current 8-bit system will be sufficient and what change would need to be made if it is not.
questions.rubric:
PART A (1 point):
Award 1 point for: 1100 1010 = 128+64+8+2 = 202.

PART B (2 points):
Award 1 point for the correct answer: 256 unique IDs (2^8 = 256).
Award 1 point for explaining: with 8 bits each position can be 0 or 1, giving 2 possible values per position. With 8 positions, there are 2^8 = 256 possible combinations, representing IDs from 0 to 255.

PART C (2 points):
Award 1 point for explaining the current system is insufficient: 8 bits can only represent 256 values (0-255), which is not enough for 300 students.
Award 1 point for the needed change: the system would need to use more bits — for example 9 bits can represent 2^9 = 512 unique IDs, which would be sufficient for 300 students.

questions.stimulus:
A city government has collected the following data about residents:
- Name and address
- Annual income
- Type of housing (rented or owned)
- Distance from nearest public transit stop

A data analyst wants to identify which neighborhoods have the highest concentration of low-income residents who live far from public transit.
questions.question: Describe in detail an algorithm a program could use to identify these neighborhoods. Your description must be detailed enough for someone else to write the program code.
questions.rubric:
Award 1 point for describing a filtering step: filter residents whose annual income is below a defined threshold AND whose distance from transit exceeds a defined distance.
Award 1 point for describing a grouping step: group the filtered residents by neighborhood.
Award 1 point for describing a counting or comparing step: count the number of qualifying residents in each neighborhood.
Award 1 point for describing an output step: sort neighborhoods by count from highest to lowest and output the top neighborhoods.
Example: Step 1 — Filter residents with income below a threshold AND distance from transit greater than a set distance. Step 2 — Group filtered residents by neighborhood. Step 3 — Count qualifying residents in each neighborhood. Step 4 — Sort neighborhoods by count from highest to lowest. Step 5 — Output the neighborhoods at the top of the list as the areas with the highest concentration.

questions.stimulus: Identify an example output of a program that processes data. Explain how this output shows an aspect of the program's functionality.
questions.question: Identify an example output of a program that processes data. Explain how this output shows an aspect of the program's functionality.
questions.rubric:
Award 1 point for identifying a valid data processing program output. Examples: a spreadsheet displaying the average of a column of numbers; a weather app displaying a forecast generated from sensor data; a recommendation algorithm outputting a list of suggested songs; a chart showing sales trends over time.
Award 1 point for explaining how the output shows functionality — the explanation must connect the specific output to what the program does with data.
Example: A music streaming app displays a list of 'Recommended Songs' as output. This shows that the program processes data about the user's listening history, compares it to data about other users with similar tastes, and outputs personalized recommendations — demonstrating the program's ability to extract insight and knowledge from user data.

questions.stimulus:
A school district is collecting data about student performance to identify students who need additional support. A teacher raises two concerns:
1. Some students enter their names differently each time (e.g., 'Jon Smith', 'John Smith', 'J. Smith')
2. The district only collects data from students who attend regularly — students who frequently miss school are underrepresented
questions.question:
Part A: Identify what type of data challenge the teacher's first concern represents. Describe what process should be used to address it.

Part B: Identify what type of data challenge the teacher's second concern represents. Explain why collecting more data from the same students would not solve this problem.
questions.rubric:
PART A (2 points):
Award 1 point for identifying the first concern as a data cleaning challenge — the data is not uniform because the same student's name is recorded differently.
Award 1 point for describing data cleaning: the process of making data uniform without changing its meaning — replacing all equivalent variations of a student's name with the same standard format.

PART B (2 points):
Award 1 point for identifying the second concern as a bias problem — the data source only represents students who attend regularly, not all students.
Award 1 point for explaining why more data from the same source won't help: bias is not eliminated by simply collecting more data. Collecting more data from regularly attending students does not add any information about frequently absent students — the source itself is biased. To address this, the district would need to collect data from a different or broader source.

questions.stimulus: Describe one piece of documentation that would be appropriate to include with a data analysis program. Explain how this documentation can be used by another programmer to better understand a particular code segment in the program.
questions.question: Describe one piece of documentation that would be appropriate to include with a data analysis program. Explain how this documentation can be used by another programmer to better understand a particular code segment in the program.
questions.rubric:
Award 1 point for describing a valid piece of documentation. Accept any of: a comment explaining what a filtering or transformation function does and what parameters it accepts; documentation describing the expected format of input data; an explanation of what the program outputs and how to interpret the results; acknowledgement of external data sources or libraries used.
Award 1 point for explaining how it helps another programmer understand the code segment.
Example: A comment above the data cleaning function that describes what format the input data must be in, what transformations are applied, and what the cleaned output looks like would be appropriate documentation. Another programmer could use this to understand exactly what data the function expects and what it produces, making it easier to use the function correctly or modify it without introducing errors.
